reviews.title: Feels like one continuous world
reviews.text:
The best part of this game is that conversations actually connect. What I say to one character carries into how other characters react to me. It’s not fragmented like most life sims, where every interaction resets. It genuinely feels like I’m living in one continuous world instead of jumping between separate scripted branches.
I also really love the custom events feature. Being able to write my own chapters instead of just picking from set options gives me real creative control over my story. I’ve spent real money on energy packs specifically for this, and it’s been worth it.
Really excited to see what’s next for this game🥰

reviews.title: Good game/ terrible energy system
reviews.text:
My biggest Takeaway from playing this game over the last few days is that the energy system is basically nonexistent. The game gives you the option to watch videos to get two energy at a time and generally you need at least three energy to do anything. The game says you get free energy allotted to you once per day. It’s been three days so far and I’ve yet to get any energy. The only energy I’ve gotten is from watching ads and even that has a cap. The game only allows you to watch so many ads.

Hopefully this is something they fix because right now the energy system just seems to be completely broken. This is a pretty fun game that analyzes the way you respond to the AI. And I can see why someone would want to spend money on this game however, the way it’s set up right now. I’m not sure I’ll be keeping the game. There’s no incentive for me personally to want to spend money on the game. I’m not going to buy energy when it’s clear. The game isn’t even giving me any energy daily to want to play the game. Where is the incentive at?

NoMi is such a fun and entertaining game! I really enjoy the overall concept, and it’s the kind of game that keeps you coming back because there’s always something new to do. The gameplay is engaging, the design is enjoyable, and it’s easy to get invested once you start playing.

reviews.title: Great app ruined by bribing users for 5-star reviews
reviews.text:
What I love:
The core concept is awesome and I immediately had high hopes. It’s so immersive and realistic, the responses arrive quickly and make logical sense, the system of analyzing my responses to interpret and explain my personality traits has been accurate and interesting. This is absolutely the kind of app I would adore and maybe pay for (which I rarely do). 

What I don’t love:
It provides little to no context about the scenarios into which it drops you, giving you 5 turns to achieve a goal in a conversation when you don’t even know what your relationship to these characters is supposed to be. That’s stressful and unpleasant, and it feels like I’m in Quantum Leap. 

The dealbreakers:
I struggled to locate a way to contact anyone to ask questions or send feedback. The contact info is a discord link that, for me, opens discord but leads nowhere. Eventually i found a link to their discord on some other site. Eventually I also found a contact email, which was on another site and, for me, buried at the bottom beneath overlapping text. It’s probably not purposeful, but it was unsettling how difficult it was to reach out. 

The biggest issue for me was that they offer free energy in exchange for a 5-star review, which I understand is against the App Store rules. Incentivizing reviews in itself isn’t a problem, but requiring them to be 5-star reviews artificially inflates the ratings and is not okay. I would have been okay with the other issues I had, but this is dishonest and not in good faith. 

I do appreciate the intensely hard work of independent developers. This app is such a wonderful concept and has so much potential. Even with unfinished features, it’s an excellent experience. But the lack of transparency regarding contact information and the manipulation of the rating system really ruined this for me. 
Please consider discontinuing the incentivized review practice. It’s such a good app on its own, it doesn’t even need the falsely inflated reviews.

reviews.title: Not Bad but Room for Improvement
reviews.text:
As the title suggests, the game isn’t half bad considering I came in with rather low expectations given I’ve been on a “download and delete” spree. Some of the things the “therapist” pointed out proved to be rather insightful, picking up patterns in myself I haven’t even noticed and at the same time validating feelings I got while recommending me things to try out. That’s probably my favorite aspect of the game. The events/scenarios are short scenarios where you’re placed with a character and assigned a goal to complete within 5 turns. Since it’s pretty randomized, some of the goals will feel out of place with the setting and or conversation (the character starts talking first so you have to continue off that). You can get up to 24 energy a day by watching ads and each event costs about 5 energy to do, so an average of 5 events a day assuming you don’t talk to the therapist. Plenty if you just want to sink 1-2 hours a day. 

What rubs me wrong though is the fact that if you do want more energy, you’d be given a prompt to join their discord and from there you are given an offer to review the game for 5 stars in order to get 30 free energy. I won’t say anything more on that, just a heads up to others considering downloading the game: take the 5 star reviews with a grain of salt. I don’t doubt there are people who genuinely thinks this game is worth the full mark but given the fact that there were at least a couple hundred threads in their “reviews for energy” channel, there’s probably a good chunk of 5 star reviews that are skewed.
